name: Databricks
description: Call the Databricks SQL Statement Execution, SQL Warehouses, Jobs, Model Serving, and Vector Search REST APIs from a BPMN process.

properties.description: Binds the element to the REST protocol connector job worker.

properties.label: Workspace URL

pattern.message: Must be an https URL, a FEEL expression, or a {{secrets.NAME}} placeholder

properties.tooltip: Base URL of the Databricks workspace. Do not include a path, the operation-specific path is appended automatically. A trailing slash is tolerated.

properties.label: Databricks API
properties.tooltip: Which Databricks API to call. The operation list below changes to match.

properties.label: Type
properties.tooltip: OAuth M2M with a service principal is the recommended method for production. See Databricks OAuth M2M.

properties.label: Client ID
properties.tooltip: Application ID of the Databricks service principal.

properties.label: Client secret
properties.tooltip: OAuth secret of the service principal. Reference it as a connector secret rather than entering the value directly.

properties.label: Personal access token
properties.description: Note: intended for testing only. Use OAuth M2M in production.
Workspace-level OAuth token endpoint, derived from the workspace URL.
properties.value: =(if ends with(databricksHostInput, "/") then substring(databricksHostInput, 1, string length(databricksHostInput) - 1) else databricksHostInput) + "/oidc/v1/token"

properties.description: Databricks requires the client credentials as a Basic Auth header.
Grants access to every Databricks REST API the principal is permitted to call.

properties.label: Messages
properties.tooltip: List of chat messages. Each entry needs a role of system, user, or assistant, and a content string.

properties.label: Max tokens

pattern.message: Must be a positive integer, or a FEEL expression

properties.tooltip: Leave blank to use the endpoint default. Databricks reserves tokens up front, so an oversized value can be rejected with HTTP 429 before the request is processed.

properties.label: Temperature

pattern.message: Must be between 0.0 and 2.0, or a FEEL expression

properties.tooltip: Leave blank to use the endpoint default of 1.0.

properties.label: Additional chat parameters
properties.tooltip: Extra parameters merged into the request body, for anything not exposed as its own field: top_p, top_k, tools, tool_choice, response_format, logprobs, reasoning_effort. Streaming stays disabled and cannot be re-enabled here.

properties.label: Request payload
properties.tooltip: Full request body for a custom model endpoint, using exactly one of dataframe_split, dataframe_records, inputs, or instances. Prefer dataframe_split, because dataframe_records does not guarantee column ordering. See Model Serving query API.

properties.label: SQL statement
properties.description: Warning: bind values as parameters below. Never concatenate process variables into this text. Maximum statement size 16 MiB.
properties.value: SELECT * FROM samples.nyctaxi.trips WHERE fare_amount > :min_fare LIMIT 10
properties.tooltip: Named markers such as :min_fare are supported. Positional question-mark markers are not supported by the Databricks SQL Statement Execution API.

properties.label: Statement parameters
properties.tooltip: List of name, value, and type entries, and the only injection-safe way to pass values into the statement. The name omits the leading colon, type defaults to STRING, and omitting value binds NULL. Complex types such as ARRAY, MAP, and STRUCT are not supported.

properties.label: Wait timeout
properties.tooltip: How long to wait inline for the statement to finish. 0s returns immediately. If the statement does not finish within the window, the response carries a non-terminal state and the result must be polled with the Get statement operation.

choices.name: CONTINUE - keep running, poll for the result
CANCEL - cancel the statement on timeout

properties.label: Disposition
properties.tooltip: How results are returned. INLINE embeds rows in the response and is capped at 25 MiB, and exceeding the cap aborts the statement without a result set. EXTERNAL_LINKS returns presigned URLs that expire after 15 minutes and must be fetched without an Authorization header.

choices.name: INLINE - rows in the response (max 25 MiB)

properties.label: Statement ID
properties.tooltip: The statement_id returned by the Execute statement operation. Statements are removed roughly 12 hours after reaching a terminal state, after which these calls return HTTP 404.

properties.label: Chunk index

pattern.message: Must be a non-negative integer, or a FEEL expression

properties.tooltip: Zero-based chunk index, taken from next_chunk_index in a previous response. Use this to page through a result set larger than one chunk.

properties.label: Warehouse ID
properties.tooltip: Start and stop return immediately. Poll Get warehouse until state is RUNNING or STOPPED before relying on the change.

properties.label: Job ID

pattern.message: Must be a non-negative integer, or a FEEL expression

properties.tooltip: Numeric ID of the Databricks job to trigger.

properties.label: Job parameters
properties.tooltip: Key-value parameters passed to the run, for example {environment: "prod"}. Keys must match parameters declared on the job.

properties.label: Idempotency token
properties.description: Note: without a token, a connector retry can start the job a second time. Databricks accepts at most 64 characters.

pattern.message: Databricks accepts at most 64 characters, or use a FEEL expression

properties.tooltip: Databricks returns the existing run instead of starting a new one when a token is reused. Deriving it from a process variable makes the trigger safe to retry. The literal-value check cannot see through a FEEL expression, so make sure what it evaluates to also stays within 64 characters -- a process instance key is fine, a concatenation of several ids may not be.

properties.label: Run ID

pattern.message: Must be a non-negative integer, or a FEEL expression

properties.tooltip: The run_id returned by Run job now. Exception: for Get run output on a multi-task job, Databricks only accepts a single task's run_id -- read it from the terminal Get run response's tasks[].run_id, not this top-level run_id.

properties.label: Index name
properties.tooltip: Three-level Unity Catalog name of the vector search index.

properties.label: Query payload
properties.tooltip: Request body for the index query. columns is required, but so is exactly one of query_text or query_vector -- a columns-only payload is rejected with HTTP 400 INVALID_PARAMETER_VALUE. Use query_text for a Delta Sync index backed by a model endpoint, or query_vector for a Direct Vector Access index or a Delta Sync index with self-managed vectors. Optional fields: num_results, filters_json, query_type, and score_threshold.

properties.label: Additional HTTP headers
properties.tooltip: Extra headers to send with the request. The User-Agent required for Databricks partner attribution is set by this template and cannot be overridden here.

properties.description: GET for read operations, POST for everything else.
Workspace URL plus the operation-specific path. Model Serving invocations have no /api/2.0 prefix.
properties.value: =(if ends with(databricksHostInput, "/") then substring(databricksHostInput, 1, string length(databricksHostInput) - 1) else databricksHostInput) + (if operationInput = "sql.execute" then "/api/2.0/sql/statements" else if operationInput = "sql.getStatement" then "/api/2.0/sql/statements/" + statementIdInput else if operationInput = "sql.cancel" then "/api/2.0/sql/statements/" + statementIdInput + "/cancel" else if operationInput = "sql.getChunk" then "/api/2.0/sql/statements/" + statementIdInput + "/result/chunks/" + string(chunkIndexInput) else if operationInput = "warehouse.get" then "/api/2.0/sql/warehouses/" + warehouseIdInput else if operationInput = "warehouse.start" then "/api/2.0/sql/warehouses/" + warehouseIdInput + "/start" else if operationInput = "warehouse.stop" then "/api/2.0/sql/warehouses/" + warehouseIdInput + "/stop" else if operationInput = "jobs.runNow" then "/api/2.2/jobs/run-now" else if operationInput = "jobs.getRun" then "/api/2.2/jobs/runs/get" else if operationInput = "jobs.getRunOutput" then "/api/2.2/jobs/runs/get-output" else if operationInput = "jobs.cancelRun" then "/api/2.2/jobs/runs/cancel" else if operationInput = "serving.getEndpoint" then "/api/2.0/serving-endpoints/" + servingEndpointNameInput else if operationInput = "vectorSearch.query" then "/api/2.0/vector-search/indexes/" + vectorIndexNameInput + "/query" else "/serving-endpoints/" + servingEndpointNameInput + "/invocations")

properties.description: The Jobs run endpoints take run_id as a query parameter rather than a path segment.
properties.value: =if operationInput = "jobs.getRun" or operationInput = "jobs.getRunOutput" then {run_id: string(runIdInput)} else null

properties.description: User-Agent is merged last, with any case-insensitive user-agent key stripped first, so the partner attribution value cannot be overridden by additional headers.
properties.value: =context merge(concatenate((for e in get entries(if additionalHeadersInput = null then {} else additionalHeadersInput) return if lower case(e.key) = "user-agent" then {} else context put({}, e.key, e.value)), [{"User-Agent": "Camunda_DatabricksConnector/1.0"}]))

properties.description: Operation-specific request body. Null optional fields are omitted, GET operations send no body, and for chat stream is merged last so it stays false.
properties.value: =if operationInput = "sql.execute" then context merge([ {statement: sqlStatementTextInput, warehouse_id: sqlWarehouseIdInput, wait_timeout: sqlWaitTimeoutInput, on_wait_timeout: sqlOnWaitTimeoutInput, disposition: sqlDispositionInput, format: "JSON_ARRAY"}, if sqlCatalogInput = null then {} else {catalog: sqlCatalogInput}, if sqlSchemaInput = null then {} else {schema: sqlSchemaInput}, if sqlParametersInput = null then {} else {parameters: sqlParametersInput}]) else if operationInput = "serving.chat" then context merge([ if chatExtraParamsInput = null then {} else chatExtraParamsInput, if chatMaxTokensInput = null then {} else {max_tokens: chatMaxTokensInput}, if chatTemperatureInput = null then {} else {temperature: chatTemperatureInput}, {messages: chatMessagesInput, stream: false}]) else if operationInput = "serving.raw" then servingRawPayloadInput else if operationInput = "jobs.runNow" then context merge([{job_id: jobIdInput}, if jobParametersInput = null then {} else {job_parameters: jobParametersInput}, if idempotencyTokenInput = null then {} else {idempotency_token: idempotencyTokenInput}]) else if operationInput = "jobs.cancelRun" then {run_id: runIdInput} else if operationInput = "vectorSearch.query" then vectorQueryPayloadInput else if list contains(["sql.cancel", "warehouse.start", "warehouse.stop"], operationInput) then {} else null

properties.label: Read timeout in seconds
properties.tooltip: Must exceed the SQL wait timeout. Model Serving allows up to 597 seconds of model execution per request, so raise this for slow inference. Use 0 for an infinite timeout.

properties.label: Result variable
properties.tooltip: Name of the process variable that receives the whole response. See result variable.

properties.label: Result expression
properties.tooltip: Maps the response into process variables, and the shape differs per operation. Execute statement returns status.state plus result.data_array, Run job now returns run_id, Get run returns state.life_cycle_state and state.result_state, and chat returns choices, where FEEL lists are 1-indexed. See result expression.

properties.label: Error expression
properties.description: Note: a failed SQL statement returns HTTP 200 with status.state FAILED, so the status code alone does not indicate success. Branch on the state with a gateway rather than here -- see the README.
properties.tooltip: Left empty on purpose. An error expression sees the mapped output whenever Result variable or Result expression is set, not the raw response, so one written against response.body silently stops firing as soon as a result mapping exists -- which is the normal way to use this task. Map status.state into a variable and branch on it with an exclusive gateway instead. If you do write an expression here, write it against whatever your result mapping produces, and remember it is evaluated on the response alone with no way to tell which operation produced it -- guard on the SQL-specific statement_id so a Model Serving raw payload carrying its own status.state is not misread as a SQL failure. Terminal SQL failure states are FAILED and CANCELED; CLOSED means "execution successful, and statement closed; result no longer available for fetch", and PENDING/RUNNING mean the statement is still executing.

properties.label: Retries
properties.description: Several operations here are non-idempotent writes (Execute statement, Run job now). A retry resends the identical request, which can duplicate a SQL INSERT/UPDATE or launch a duplicate job run. The SQL Statement Execution API has no idempotency key at all; Run job now accepts one (see Idempotency token below), but only if it is set. Defaults to 0 for that reason -- raise it only for read-only operations or once you have confirmed the mitigation covers your case.

properties.label: Retry backoff
properties.tooltip: ISO 8601 duration to wait between retries.

properties.label: Job timeout
properties.description: Must exceed Read timeout in seconds above, or Zeebe can consider the job timed out and reactivate it on another worker while this HTTP request is still in flight -- a duplicate non-idempotent call that Retries = 0 does not prevent, because it happens outside the connector.
properties.tooltip: ISO-8601 duration after which Zeebe considers this job timed out if not yet completed. Leave empty to use the default timeout. Raise this alongside Read timeout in seconds when waiting on slow Model Serving inference (up to 597s) or a long SQL wait_timeout.

properties.label: Version
properties.tooltip: Version of the element template

properties.label: ID
properties.tooltip: ID of the element template

steps.name: SQL Statement Execution
steps.description: Execute and manage Databricks SQL statements.

steps.name: Execute statement
steps.description: Run a SQL statement against a Databricks SQL warehouse (POST /api/2.0/sql/statements).

steps.name: Get statement status and result
steps.description: Poll a Databricks SQL statement's status and inline result (GET /api/2.0/sql/statements/{id}).

steps.name: Get result chunk
steps.description: Page through a Databricks SQL result set larger than one chunk (GET .../result/chunks/{index}).

steps.name: Cancel statement
steps.description: Cancel a running Databricks SQL statement (POST .../cancel).

steps.name: SQL Warehouses
steps.description: Manage Databricks SQL warehouse state.

steps.name: Get warehouse
steps.description: Read a Databricks SQL warehouse's current state (GET /api/2.0/sql/warehouses/{id}).

steps.name: Start warehouse
steps.description: Start a stopped Databricks SQL warehouse (POST .../start).

steps.name: Stop warehouse
steps.description: Stop a running Databricks SQL warehouse (POST .../stop).

steps.name: Jobs
steps.description: Trigger and monitor Databricks job runs.

steps.name: Run job now
steps.description: Trigger a Databricks job run now (POST /api/2.2/jobs/run-now).

steps.name: Get run
steps.description: Read a Databricks job run's status (GET /api/2.2/jobs/runs/get).

steps.name: Get run output
steps.description: Read a completed Databricks job run's task output (GET /api/2.2/jobs/runs/get-output).

steps.name: Cancel run
steps.description: Cancel an in-progress Databricks job run (POST /api/2.2/jobs/runs/cancel).

steps.name: Model Serving
steps.description: Invoke and inspect Databricks Model Serving endpoints.

steps.name: Invoke chat / LLM endpoint
steps.description: Send a chat completion request to a Databricks Model Serving endpoint.

steps.name: Invoke custom model, raw payload
steps.description: Send a raw request body to a custom Databricks Model Serving endpoint.

steps.name: Get endpoint
steps.description: Read a Databricks Model Serving endpoint's status (GET /api/2.0/serving-endpoints/{name}).

steps.name: Vector Search
steps.description: Query a Databricks Vector Search index.

steps.name: Query index
steps.description: Query a Databricks Vector Search index (POST /api/2.0/vector-search/indexes/{name}/query).
